standard.title: Comparing data displays
standard.description: Analyse the effectiveness of different displays or visualisations in illustrating and comparing data distributions, then discuss the shape of distributions and the variation in the data
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can create and compare different graphical representations (AC9M3ST02). They have not yet analysed the relative effectiveness of different displays or discussed distribution shape and variation.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students analyse the effectiveness of different data displays, discuss distribution shape and identify variation in data.

nodes.label: Comparing display types
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can compare two or more data displays of the same data and identify differences in what each communicates effectively.
nodes.minimum_width: Compare two different displays of the same dataset; identify one way each display is more or less useful for answering a particular question.
nodes.typical_width: Compare student-generated and digital displays of the same data; describe similarities and differences; comment on usefulness for different questions; interpret representations from media where symbols represent one-to-many relationships.
wider: Evaluate data representations from news sources or online media, asking 'what questions can this display answer?' and 'what information does it obscure or distort?'
Investigate how AI developers use data visualisation as a step in data preparation, connecting data analysis to real-world AI applications
success_criteria: Students can compare two displays of the same data and describe at least one advantage of each for a specific purpose
Students can suggest at least one question that can be answered by a given display

nodes.label: Distribution shape and variation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can discuss the shape of a data distribution and describe the variation in the data.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe one feature of a distribution's shape (e.g. which category has the most data, whether values are spread out or clustered).
nodes.typical_width: Discuss the shape of distributions using informal language (spread out, clustered, even); identify the highest and lowest frequency categories; describe variation — how much the values differ; comment on what the distribution suggests about the original question.
wider: Compare distributions from two different data sets on the same question (e.g. survey results from two different classes) and describe the differences in shape and variation
Investigate what happens to a distribution when the sample size changes — collecting data in two rounds and comparing the distributions

response_modes.reason: Discussing distribution shape requires students to move beyond individual data points to see the aggregate pattern. The reasoning scaffold — 'look at the whole shape first, then describe where the data clusters' — must be made explicit to shift from point-by-point reading to pattern recognition.

success_criteria: Students can describe the overall shape of a distribution using informal language
Students can identify and describe the variation in a data set (whether values are spread out or clustered)
